question: What is the size of this dataset?

evidence: This paper fills this gap by analyzing intent classification performance with a focus on out-of-scope handling. To do so, we constructed a new dataset with 23,700 queries that are short and unstructured, in the same style made by real users of task-oriented systems. The queries cover 150 intents, plus out-of-scope queries that do not fall within any of the 150 in-scope intents.

answer.free_form_answer: 23,700 queries, including 22,500 in-scope queries covering 150 intents, which can be grouped into 10 general domains and 1,200 out-of-scope queries.
evidence: We introduce a new crowdsourced dataset of 23,700 queries, including 22,500 in-scope queries covering 150 intents, which can be grouped into 10 general domains. The dataset also includes 1,200 out-of-scope queries. Table TABREF2 shows examples of the data.

title: An Evaluation Dataset for Intent Classification and Out-of-Scope Prediction
answer_short: 100 training, 20 validation, and 30 testing queries per intent
answer_rationale: Text 3 explicitly states that for each intent, there are 100 training queries, 20 validation queries, and 30 testing queries. This is directly supported by the evidence and matches the reasoning trace.
